title: Water checks: meter readings, leaks, and fixture flow
summary: Use complete billing periods and consistent units to track water. Check for visible leaks and measure fixture flow before choosing a change.
content:
Record water quantities from a meter or bill and keep the billing dates and units. One kilolitre (kL) equals 1,000 litres (L). Compare like-for-like periods; a partial period is not directly comparable to a full month.

Check taps, toilet cisterns, and visible pipework for leaks. A bucket and timer can measure fixture flow in litres per minute. Record the test conditions and repeat it if readings vary.

Do not assume a fixture change will reduce total use. Actual results depend on the fixture, usage, water pressure, and user behaviour. EcoTwin does not supply local water tariffs or estimate savings from a photo.
applicability_conditions: Has a water meter, bill, or a fixture whose flow can be measured
implementation_steps: Enter a complete-period meter or bill quantity with its original unit
Check visible fixtures for leaks and record any repair
Use a bucket and timer to measure fixture flow
Compare only periods with matching dates and units
limitations: Unmetered tanker or borewell use may not have a reliable quantity
Flow measurement does not by itself establish water savings
